label: Aristotle, Metaphysics IV.7, 1012a24-28: Denial of excluded middle: for some proposition p…
interpretation: Attribution reading: Aristotle reports, and rejects, that Anaxagoras' account seems to posit something between the two sides of a contradiction, so that it makes everything false: when things are mixed, the mixture is neither good nor not good. The claim records the view Aristotle ascribes to Anaxagoras (hedged by 'seems', ἔοικε), not a view Aristotle holds, and not a judgement on what Anaxagoras himself wrote. Formalized as the existence of a proposition p with neither p nor ¬p, i.e. ¬(p ∨ ¬p).
